problem: Autoregressive differentiable planners (VIN/QMDP-net/CALVIN) are myopic and data-hungry, while diffusion policies are behavior-cloning based, assume full observability or a known goal, and fail on situations outside expert demonstrations (e.g., dead ends) under partial observability.
motivation: Navigation under partial observability needs foresight and the ability to explore/backtrack, but experts demonstrate with full observability so cloning never sees dead ends. 3D real data is scarce, whereas 2D maze data is abundant, so transferring a 2D policy to 3D would save training cost.
key_idea: Combine a diffusion plan generator with a QMDP-based differentiable value function (with state estimation) that selects the best of multiple sampled plans (with best-plan backtracking), and transfer the 2D-trained policy zero-shot to 3D by projecting segmented RGB-D point clouds to BEV grid maps.
insight: Value guidance is the key ingredient: replacing voting with multi-step Q-value selection lifts success from 0.114 to 0.538 on GridMaze2D (0.082 to 0.542 on AVD), and best-plan memory adds a further jump to 0.906. Plain Diffusion Policy (behavior cloning) nearly fails in partially observable mazes (0.060), showing cloning cannot handle dead ends unseen in expert data. Removing the semantic-segmentation BEV projector drops AVD success from 0.776 to 0.486, showing the projection makes 2D-to-3D transfer work.
method: Diffusion plan generator: 1D U-Net conditional DDPM (32 steps) generating action trajectories (prediction horizon 4, execution 2, receding horizon) conditioned via FiLM on a partial environment map encoded by a CNN; actions bit-encoded as analog bits.
QMDP value function with state estimation: Bayesian filter (learned translation-invariant transition and observation correction) plus K=60 value-iteration convolutions; Q soft-indexed by the belief.
Action-validity reward: learns action logits and a threshold, with soft-thresholded valid-action mask A-hat merging reward R_m for valid and large-negative R_f for invalid actions.
Value-guided plan selection: sample L=24 plans in parallel and choose the one with highest average belief-weighted multi-step Q value.

Best plan candidate backtracking: keep the previously selected best plan (executed actions removed) in the candidate set so receding-horizon replanning cannot overwrite an optimal plan; inference only.

2D-to-3D projection: build a point cloud from RGB-D, segment it with pre-trained Swin3D (13 classes), project to a 50x50 BEV grid where floor/ceiling-majority cells are free and others obstacles, and feed it to the 2D-trained policy zero-shot.
Retrained variant: add egocentric RGB features concatenated with the BEV map, trained on limited AVD demonstrations.

setting.backbone: 1D conv U-Net diffusion policy + CNN encoder + QMDP value iteration network (trained from scratch); pre-trained Swin3D for point cloud segmentation
setting.training_data: Expert A* trajectories in randomly generated 2D mazes (15x15 for GridMaze2D; 30x30 model for AVD zero-shot); AVD retrain uses leave-one-scene-out cross-validation on the AVD scenes
setting.observation: Partial 2D grid map (3 channels) in mazes; egocentric RGB-D converted to a BEV grid via point cloud and segmentation in AVD (optionally plus RGB features)
setting.simulator: GridMaze2D (custom synthetic) and Active Vision Dataset (real image streams, 30cm grid, 30° rotation)
setting.privileged: Expert demonstrations use goal location knowledge (A*) at training time only; camera pose is used to build the point cloud; no privileged info claimed at test time

numbers_note: Success rates printed as fractions (0-1) and converted to percent; no standard VLN/ObjectNav benchmark used.
results: On GridMaze2D the method reaches 0.906 SR at 15x15 (vr=2) vs CALVIN 0.855 and Diffusion Policy 0.060, and 0.624 at 30x30 vs CALVIN 0.326. On AVD, zero-shot 2D-to-3D transfer gets 0.679 mean SR (CALVIN-2D 0.635, CALVIN-3D 0.682), and retraining with RGB gets 0.706.
limitations: Relies heavily on accurate point cloud semantic segmentation; mislabeling causes wrong BEV maps and planning errors.
QMDP assumes full observability after the current step, making long-horizon values suboptimal, which is amplified by multi-step plans.
Evaluation is limited to synthetic mazes and a small AVD subset (8 scenes, one object) with no real robot and no standard VLN/ObjectNav benchmarks.
